runs.information: Added benchmark run metadata, workbook ID writes, and automatic Koppen image export; climate simulation parameters and generation logic unchanged.

Scaled moisture-advection iterations, maritime fetch distance, ocean sampling, and continental fetch normalization with map resolution; all climate strengths, circulation, temperature heuristics, and Koppen thresholds unchanged.

Normalized per-iteration moisture source, retention, condensation, and overflow after run 3 exposed iteration-count coupling; retained resolution-scaled 90 iterations, 143-cell maritime fetch, 24-cell ocean sampling, and 239-cell continental fetch normalization; other climate logic unchanged.

Tightened the D-climate dry-winter classification from a 1:4 to 1:10 driest-cold/wettest-warm precipitation ratio; added pixelwise spatial accuracy and kappa reporting plus benchmark-only black sea/lake/EF rendering; moisture transport and all temperature/rainfall generation unchanged.

Applied existing continental winter-cooling and summer-warming strengths and caps to the seasonal temperature fields used by final Koppen classification; retained the run 5 1:10 D winter-dry rule, resolution-scaled moisture transport, spatial metrics, and black benchmark backgrounds; no new climate strengths or thresholds.
Added reference-Dfc spatial confusion and seasonal temperature/rainfall driver diagnostics; climate simulation parameters, physical generation, Koppen rules, and benchmark rendering unchanged.

Repeated the unchanged diagnostic baseline with detailed climate-error reporting enabled to capture reference-Dfc driver summaries and measure run-to-run stability; simulation parameters and logic unchanged.

Allowed existing upwind-ocean maritime moisture to enter the advection source over subfreezing land while retaining zero local frozen-land evaporation; diagnostics, Koppen rules, all tuning strengths, and temperature logic unchanged.
Added reference-class confusion summaries for simulated BWk and Af pixels to identify which real climate regions drive both excesses; climate simulation parameters and logic unchanged from run 9.

Replaced non-conserving per-land-cell upwind ocean moisture injection with conservative wind advection; doubled transport substeps from 30 to 60 baseline cells while keeping total evaporation, retention, and condensation duration normalized to 30 physical iterations; land evaporation and Koppen rules unchanged.

Conserved non-precipitated atmospheric moisture by removing the generic 0.996 per-physical-iteration carry decay (11.3% loss over the 30-iteration duration); retained run 11 conservative 60-cell transport, ocean and land source strengths, condensation physics, and Koppen rules.

Restored the run 10 moisture transport baseline and gated its unresolved upwind maritime land source by resolved seasonal surface pressure: full strength at neutral or low pressure, tapering to zero at a +24 pressure anomaly; all other moisture and Koppen parameters unchanged.

Ablation experiment: restored run 10 transport and maritime-source behavior, but disabled the temperature-only land evaporation source to test whether unlimited warm-land water creation causes excessive Af; no other climate parameters or Koppen rules changed.

Kept the run 14 removal of unlimited temperature-only land evaporation and increased unresolved upwind maritime moisture from 0.16 to 0.24 to test ocean-derived recovery of continental humidity; all resolved ocean evaporation, transport, condensation, and Koppen settings unchanged.

Replaced unlimited temperature-only land evaporation with water-limited evapotranspiration: rainfall infiltrates a finite 80-unit soil store at 65%, and temperature sets potential evaporation but actual evaporation cannot exceed stored water; retained run 15 maritime transport and all other settings.

Retained run 16 finite soil-water evapotranspiration and increased unresolved upwind maritime moisture from 0.24 to 0.32 as a controlled transport calibration for cold continental interiors; all other climate and Koppen settings unchanged.

Replaced inland maritime moisture creation and generic atmospheric loss with a conservative ocean-atmosphere-soil-runoff budget; replaced linear moisture capacity and forced condensation rates with Buck saturation vapour pressure, hydrostatic surface pressure, and uplift/subsidence parcel cooling; added WorldClim monthly temperature and precipitation validation.

Kept the run 18 closed thermodynamic water cycle and replaced one-cell moisture transport with conservative operator-split advection using model wind speed, latitude-dependent Earth grid-cell dimensions, and a three-hour timestep; corrected WorldClim precipitation NoData handling.

Retained run 19 conservative wind-speed advection and increased the physical transport timestep from three to six hours to test realistic continental moisture penetration; fixed the legacy annual precipitation CSV representation of reference NoData cells.

Selected the run 19 three-hour conservative advection timestep after the six-hour experiment reduced monthly precipitation correlation and Koppen spatial agreement; retained corrected WorldClim NoData handling and all closed-budget thermodynamics.

Finalized phase-1 validation without changing simulation output: added cosine-latitude area-weighted Koppen, temperature, and precipitation metrics; restricted the legacy annual precipitation comparison to cells that are land in both the simulation and WorldClim; retained the selected three-hour conservative water transport.

Replaced empirical latitude-band temperatures with daily orbital insolation, temperature-dependent snow and sea-ice albedo, calibrated linear outgoing longwave radiation, globally conservative atmospheric heat redistribution, and distinct land/ocean heat capacities; preserved four physical seasonal states and removed rainfall-temperature, distance-to-coast seasonal-amplification, and subpolar-class cleanup heuristics.

Refined the energy model after run 23: separated conservative meridional heat transport from same-latitude land-ocean air exchange so surface air couples locally to the ocean mixed layer without flattening the planetary latitude gradient; added land, ocean, and elevation temperature diagnostics.

Increased conservative same-latitude land-ocean air exchange after run 24 showed a 4.84 C pre-elevation land-ocean split, and used the same cloud-effective open-surface albedo for land and ocean while retaining snow and sea-ice feedbacks.

Rebalanced run 25's overdamped surface exchange: used moderate same-latitude land-ocean coupling, stronger globally conservative poleward heat transport, reduced cloud-effective snow albedo, and converged the longwave calibration to the configured mean temperature.

Selected modest meridional transport after run 26 over-warmed polar rows, used vegetation-like clear-sky land albedo with cloud-effective snow feedback, and removed the later relief/uplift surface-cooling pass because elevation lapse is already applied by the energy model and uplift cooling belongs in condensation physics.

Doubled the effective land-column heat capacity after run 27 revealed 112,832 Dfd cells from excessive high-latitude seasonal range; all orbital, radiative, albedo, transport, and water-cycle physics otherwise unchanged.

Raised conservative meridional heat transport from 3 to 4 W m-2 K-1 to reduce run 28's excess ET/EF while retaining the successful 4e7 J m-2 K-1 land thermal inertia; increased longwave-calibration iterations so the configured global mean converges.

Selected the run 28 energy architecture after the run 29 transport increase worsened spatial and monthly metrics: retained 3 W m-2 K-1 conservative meridional transport, 4e7 J m-2 K-1 land thermal inertia, physical elevation lapse, explicit four-season temperatures, and converged longwave calibration.

Activated coupled lower-layer mass continuity: surface pressure now responds to ascent and subsidence with diffusion and area-weighted atmospheric mass correction; surface winds and divergence are recomputed during each two-layer circulation iteration; the thermally positioned Gaussian pressure-belt seed is retained for isolation.

Removed all prescribed Gaussian equatorial-low, subtropical-high, subpolar-low, and polar-high pressure belts. Surface pressure is initialized only from resolved thermal anomalies, land-ocean contrast, seasonality, and elevation, then coupled to vertical mass redistribution and diffusion; all coupling coefficients remain unchanged from run 31.

Replaced empirical wind scaling with a unit-aware two-layer atmosphere: 1000-to-500 hPa geopotential thickness follows the hypsometric equation; winds solve steady pressure-gradient, Coriolis, and Rayleigh-drag momentum balance on physical grid spacing; vertical motion follows lower/upper mass continuity in hPa per day; surface pressure follows column divergence with bounded physical tendencies. Added aligned WorldClim monthly 10 m wind-speed validation.

Calibrated the unit-aware atmosphere after run 33 exceeded observed monthly wind speeds: smoothed 500 hPa thermal thickness over roughly 200 km, shortened land/ocean Rayleigh drag times, limited climatological surface-pressure anomalies to 35 hPa and tendencies to 12 hPa per day, and increased horizontal mass diffusion. Equations and observed-data targets are unchanged.

Separated synoptic mass continuity from terrain-scale flow after run 34: lower and upper divergence are smoothed at the circulation scale before vertical motion and pressure tendency; topographic wind deflection and uplift are applied only after the large-scale two-layer solve converges. Strengthened physically interpretable boundary-layer drag while retaining the run 34 pressure calibration.

Fixed four-season precipitation integrity discovered after run 35: conservative moisture output is clamped before signed 16-bit storage, and the established nonlinear high-rainfall cap now applies consistently to January, April, July, and October instead of leaving transition seasons able to overflow or retain unbounded extremes. Atmospheric physics is unchanged from run 35.

Added calibrated NASA IMERG V07B annual precipitation validation at the benchmark grid resolution, with separate global, land, and ocean area-weighted diagnostics. Simulation physics is unchanged from run 36.

Removed the landform-aware rainfall blur from ocean-bearing worlds. The conservative four-season moisture solver now feeds climate classification directly and all seasons receive identical post-processing; the legacy blur remains only for airless all-land fallback worlds.

Replaced arbitrary SST-scaled moisture injection with a bulk-aerodynamic evaporation flux driven by saturation specific humidity, surface pressure, resolved wind, relative humidity, and sea ice. Each seasonal solve now represents 30 daily transport steps; land evapotranspiration is soil-water-limited, and redundant grid-space wind-convergence cooling was removed in favor of resolved vertical motion.

Calibrated the physical surface momentum balance against WorldClim 10 m wind magnitude by shortening ocean, land, and high-relief Rayleigh drag times. This reduces excessive near-surface winds without changing upper-level thermal forcing or moisture equations.

Separated evaporation wind from column moisture transport: bulk evaporation remains driven by resolved 10 m wind, while moisture advection now follows an 80/20 blend of surface and upper-layer flow as a reduced 850 hPa transport approximation. No rainfall smoothing or inland source was added.

Removed the final hard-coded latitude fallback from the legacy scalar wind layer and deleted obsolete prescribed pressure-belt tuning. Calm legacy wind directions now come from the resolved surface/lower-tropospheric transport flow, or remain calm when neither layer provides a direction; core atmosphere and moisture physics are unchanged from run 41.

Persisted atmospheric and soil moisture across the four representative seasons and iterated up to four deterministic climate cycles toward periodic storage convergence; water budgets now include initial storage. Restored EF in benchmark images and changed 0.png to write only when missing or outdated. Koppen thresholds, atmosphere, and evaporation coefficients are unchanged from run 42.

Added precipitation-distribution diagnostics before and after integer storage, cosine-area-weighted water budgets, and per-run land hydrology metrics. Climate physics and tuning remain identical to run 43: critical relative humidity is 1.0 and initial soil moisture is zero.
Isolated ablation: lowered precipitation critical relative humidity from 1.00 to 0.75; retained run-44 diagnostics; no land-surface or circulation changes.

Isolated wet-start ablation: restored precipitation critical relative humidity to 1.00 and initialized land soil moisture at full 80 mm field capacity; all other hydrology, circulation, and diagnostics unchanged.

Land-water closure experiment: retained 0.75 precipitation onset; replaced fixed 35% infiltration rejection with saturation-excess runoff, changed linear soil-moisture stress to a square-root response, and removed the extra 0.45 land evaporation multiplier; initial soil remains zero.

Corrected meridional water transport to advect area-weighted column mass on the latitude-longitude grid using exact finite-volume row areas; retained run-47 precipitation and soil-water closure; no eddy mixing yet.

Repeated run-48 area-conservative transport with lake and rift-lake cells excluded consistently from land reference validation; simulation physics unchanged, making precipitation metrics comparable again.

Added conservative deterministic transient-eddy moisture diffusion derived from lower-to-upper wind shear, Coriolis strength, and a 100 km mixing length; added no-flux handling at singular polar rows; retained run-49 mean advection, rainfall, and land-water physics.

Reduced the run-50 shear-derived eddy moisture diffusivity fourfold by changing the mixing length from 100 km to 25 km and the cap from 1,000,000 to 250,000 m2/s; all transport geometry, rainfall, and land-water physics unchanged.

Directional eddy experiment: retained run-51 shear-derived 25 km zonal mixing but disabled meridional eddy diffusivity to avoid cross-belt rainfall smearing; mean meridional advection and all other physics unchanged.

Rejected the eddy kernel and restored the run-49 moisture solver; corrected surface and upper-layer wind divergence for spherical geometry by including meridional cosine-area convergence; retained area-conservative water transport and polar boundary handling.

Increased spherical surface and upper-layer divergence smoothing from 6 to 24 grid passes to test whether unresolved grid-scale convergence noise drives precipitation intermittency; retained the run-53 hydrology, area-conservative moisture transport, and spherical divergence formulation.

Rejected run-54's 24-pass divergence smoothing and restored 6 passes; added 6-pass synoptic smoothing of the quantized lower/upper blended moisture-transport wind to suppress artificial whole-metre-per-second cell-scale flux convergence without adding moisture or changing condensation, hydrology, or vertical motion.

Rejected run-55 transport-wind smoothing and restored the run-53 transport; lowered only the condensation critical humidity from 0.75 to 0.43, equivalent to testing an approximately 12-percent cloud-bearing column against the unchanged 28-percent bulk moisture column used for evaporation.

Separated condensation regimes after run 56: restored ocean large-scale condensation to 0.75 critical relative humidity while retaining the experimentally supported 0.43 cloud-column threshold over land; evaporation capacity, transport, vertical motion, and hydrology are unchanged.

Mapped the separated land condensation response by lowering only the land critical relative humidity from 0.43 to 0.25; ocean condensation remains 0.75 and all transport, circulation, evaporation, and hydrology settings remain those of run 57.

Diagnostic baseline: retained run 58 physics and tuning; added temperature-reachability, northern 50-70N warmth and precipitation, 5-degree IMERG correlation, and rainfall-storage clipping metrics. The first thermal-signature diagnostic was later found to use the legacy two-temperature heat subtype rule; only that diagnostic is superseded by run 60.

Corrected diagnostic baseline: retained run 58 physics; thermal reachability now mirrors the four-season Koppen classifier including second-warmest temperature; repeated fixed seed 1 to quantify benchmark determinism before tuning.

Thermal-inertia experiment: reduced land heat capacity from 4.0e7 to 3.0e7 J/m2/K; eddy moisture transport remains disabled and run 60 hydrology, circulation, condensation, and diagnostics are unchanged.
Thermal-inertia bracket: reduced land heat capacity from run 60 baseline 4.0e7 to 2.5e7 J/m2/K; eddy moisture transport remains disabled and all other run 60 physics and diagnostics are unchanged.

Interaction experiment: retained run 62 land heat capacity 2.5e7 J/m2/K and added conservative transient-eddy moisture diffusion from vertical wind shear and rotation, using a 25 km mixing length and 250,000 m2/s cap; mean advection and all hydrology remain unchanged.

Interaction bracket: raised land heat capacity from run 63 2.5e7 to 3.0e7 J/m2/K while retaining the conservative shear-derived 25 km transient-eddy moisture closure; all other physics and diagnostics are unchanged.

Targeted eddy experiment: retained run 64 land heat capacity 3.0e7 and 25 km shear-derived diffusion, tapered eddy mixing smoothly from zero at 20 degrees to full strength at 45 degrees latitude, and raised maximum hydrology spinup from 4 to 8 cycles so the wetter state can converge.

Thermal-target experiment: reduced land heat capacity to 1.5e7 J/m2/K based on the full-pipeline 50-70N warmest-month response; disabled transient-eddy mixing to isolate temperature, while retaining convergent spinup and run 65 diagnostics.
Replaced the single land heat slab with an implicitly coupled 7.5e6 J/m2/K surface and 3.0e7 J/m2/K deep-soil reservoir at 1.5 W/m2/K; transient eddy moisture mixing remains disabled.

Made land snow-albedo feedback respond to row-mean terrain elevation before the lapse-rate correction, preventing elevated ice sheets from entering an artificial summer albedo runaway; retained the run 67 two-layer land thermal model and restored the ungated 25 km shear-derived conservative eddy moisture closure preferred visually from runs 63-64.

Added an emergent persistent ice-sheet albedo state: land whose elevation-adjusted deep-layer temperature remains below -4 to -14 C retains up to 0.80 ice albedo through summer. Kept the run 68 two-layer land model and ungated conservative eddy moisture transport.

Replaced fixed-step longwave calibration with a deterministic bracketed 24-pass search that retains the closest evaluated equilibrium across nonlinear ice-albedo feedback; all run 69 thermal and eddy physics are unchanged.

Diagnostic baseline with run 70 physics unchanged; added ERA5 process comparisons, IPCC AR6 regional climate diagnostics, aligned external reference preparation, and persistent per-run validation bundles.

Replaced row-mean land elevation in snow/permanent-ice albedo feedback with seven quantile samples of each latitude row's actual land-elevation distribution; retained run 70 calibration, two-layer land thermal model, eddy moisture transport, and all hydrology settings.

Replaced latitude-wide permanent land-ice feedback with a cell-local radiative response driven by each cell's elevation-adjusted persistent temperature; globally balanced the local ice forcing through longwave calibration while retaining seasonal snow, ocean ice, two-layer land thermal inertia, eddies, and hydrology.

Diagnostic and classification control on run 71 physics: corrected the temperate C dry-winter threshold from one quarter to the standard one tenth of the wettest warm-season month; added conserved atmospheric residence time, condensation activity, pressure decomposition, and temperature-threshold diagnostics without changing climate physics.

Replaced latitude-wide permanent land ice with a bounded local ice-temperature fixed point. The area-mean cell ice fraction supplies each latitude row's net albedo forcing, while zero-row-mean cell albedo responses redistribute temperatures by local elevation and deterministic terrain anomaly without post-hoc global compensation. Retained the corrected C dry-winter rule and run 74 diagnostics.

Stabilized local permanent-ice coupling after run 75. Solved the area-mean permanent-ice fraction for each latitude row from the full distribution of cell-local deep-land temperatures, jointly relaxed the longwave calibration to the configured global mean, and applied bounded zero-row-mean seasonal albedo temperature responses only after the prognostic row state converged. This removes cellwise ice-mask bistability while retaining local elevation and terrain structure.

Replaced annual/deep-temperature permanent-ice eligibility with a converged warmest-season ablation criterion. The solver now uses actual seasonal snapshots during every calibration iteration, requires five consecutive stable iterations, retains Antarctic and high-elevation ice where summers remain below the smooth -4 to -14 C transition, and permits boreal land with warm summers to shed permanent snow. Row-mean ice forcing and zero-row-mean local albedo responses remain conservative.

Added a generative ice-sheet mass-balance proxy after run 77: permanent ice survives from local warmest-season temperature, while cold land between 0.75 and 1.75 km smoothly seeds highland ice sheets from local deep-land temperature. The coupled row-mean radiative state converges for five consecutive iterations; new thermal gates reject runs before hydrology unless northern 50-70 N summer warmth and southern 60-90 S icecap eligibility are both plausible. No latitude or hemisphere-specific ice rule is used.

Added a temperature-derived axisymmetric circulation background. Hadley-cell width is computed from simulated equator-to-pole contrast using Held-Hou scaling; equatorial and subpolar lows plus subtropical and polar highs are initialized with a hydrostatic mass-redistribution amplitude. No Earth pressure map or fixed climate latitude is prescribed. IPCC diagnostics now report ET and EF separately.

Replaced threshold-excess instantaneous rainout with a smooth subgrid-cloud activation closure. Relative humidity above a dynamically adjusted critical value activates precipitation with a cubic response and an explicit two-day conversion timescale; resolved ascent lowers the critical humidity and subsidence raises it. Retained run 79's temperature-derived pressure background. No unconditional drizzle or Earth-specific climate geography is prescribed.

Rejected run 80's cubic subgrid-cloud activation because it concentrated rainfall and increased zero-rain land. Retained run 79's spatial condensation threshold and pressure background, but replaced the 0.58-day effective dump of excess column water with a conservative two-day exponential relaxation. This isolates finite condensation time without unconditional drizzle or a highly selective activation curve.

Preserved generated surface-pressure and upper-height fields in floating point between the pressure and wind stages; rounded planet maps now serve only as public storage and as a fallback for separately invoked wind stages. Added observational circulation-precision, precipitation-extreme-location, and separate budget/gridded residence-time diagnostics. Climate circulation, moisture, energy, cryosphere, and Koppen tuning parameters are unchanged from run 81.

Retained run 82's float-through circulation fields and projected surface-pressure and upper-height stationary structure onto resolved zonal wavenumbers 1-4 before the first gradient calculation and after each circulation iteration. Zonal means are preserved, while fine terrain remains represented by downstream orographic wind/uplift effects. Climate moisture, energy, cryosphere, and Koppen parameters are unchanged from run 82.

Extended run 83's pressure/upper-height stationary-wave projection to two dimensions. Zonal wavenumbers 1-4 are retained, while each mode's amplitude and phase are projected onto meridional cosine modes 0-24 to prevent independent latitude-row striping. Zonal means, float-through fields, downstream terrain uplift, and all moisture, energy, cryosphere, and Koppen parameters are unchanged.

Loosened run 84's two-dimensional stationary pressure/upper-height projection from zonal wavenumbers 1-4 to 1-8, retaining meridional modes 0-24. This brackets the resolved stationary scale while preserving zonal means, float-through fields, downstream terrain uplift, and all moisture, energy, cryosphere, and Koppen parameters.

Corrected the two-dimensional stationary pressure and upper-height projection so the zonal-mean component is projected onto meridional modes 0-24 as well as stationary zonal modes 1-8. Runs 83-85 had left the zonal mean unfiltered, allowing row-scale latitude noise to survive as horizontal climate bands. All moisture, energy, cryosphere, terrain-uplift, and Koppen parameters remain unchanged.

Replaced runs 83-86's cumulative hard projection of the full pressure and upper-height state with a non-cumulative scale-selective filter used only when deriving wind gradients. The filter resolves zonal modes 0-8 and meridional modes 0-24 while retaining 25 percent of unresolved structure; the evolving state, zonal means, moisture, energy, cryosphere, terrain uplift, and Koppen logic are otherwise unchanged.

Simulation parameters and climate logic unchanged from run 87. Added automatic benchmark export of a fixed-scale four-season mean land-temperature image in degrees C and a fixed-scale annual precipitation image in mm/year, plus a scale and reference-path description, so physical fields can be visually compared alongside Koppen classes.

Separated horizontal moisture transport from circulation adjustment. Horizontal surface and upper winds retain run 87's 25 percent unresolved pressure and height structure, while surface-pressure tendency and vertical ascent are now derived from fully projected zonal modes 0-8 and meridional modes 0-24. This targets the comb-like condensation bands revealed by run 88's annual precipitation image without reverting horizontal transport to run 86's over-zonal state.

Reduced divergence-driven vertical motion to ERA5 magnitude (0.32 response, 100 hPa/day cap) and removed the area-weighted global mean vertical mass flux each circulation iteration. This isolates the repeated zonal rainfall bands before changing terrain uplift.

Retained run 90 vertical-mass correction and disabled the unstable column-divergence-to-surface-pressure feedback. Surface circulation now remains tied to the temperature-derived pressure belts instead of amplifying base winds from about 2 to 17 m/s; this isolates the source of repeated zonal moisture-convergence bands.

Retained run 91's stable diagnostic surface circulation. Replaced dimensionless terrain uplift with wind-dot-terrain-slope parcel displacement over one grid crossing, then applied 4.0 C/km moist ascent cooling and 4.9 C/km effective lee descent warming. This tests physically signed windward rain and lee rain shadows.

Retained run 91 circulation and run 92's dimensional wind-slope lift. Accumulated slope-signed windward rise and leeward drop across the existing six-cell terrain horizon, preventing nearby but crosswind terrain from triggering lift. Added per-season orographic displacement statistics.

Retained run 91's stable surface circulation and run 93's terrain-following parcel displacement. Removed the 20 percent 500 hPa wind contribution from moisture advection because it degraded transport-wind correlations and could reverse low-level flow across major terrain. Moisture now follows the resolved boundary-layer wind pending a dedicated lower-tropospheric layer.

Retained run 91's stable pressure solve and run 93's terrain-following uplift. Preserved the better surface-wind transport direction from run 94, but removed the arbitrary 75-to-25 percent ocean-to-continent condensation-threshold drop. A uniform 75 percent finite-time column threshold now lets resolved convergence, uplift, cooling, and subsidence determine rainfall placement.

Rejected run 95's uniform condensation threshold and restored the prior inland finite-time closure. Retained surface-directed moisture transport, then added smoothed longitude-dependent surface-pressure anomalies from each row's generated land-ocean temperature contrast. Warm columns now create thermal lows and cold columns thermal highs with zero row-mean mass change, allowing the ITCZ and monsoon flow to bend around generated continents without geographic rules.

Retained run 96's row-mass-neutral temperature-derived stationary pressure and all hydrology settings. Increased only the thermal mass-redistribution efficiency from 0.12 to 0.30 so stationary pressure approaches ERA5's observed 3-5 hPa RMS. This tests whether physically stronger seasonal continental lows bend the ITCZ and draw Atlantic moisture into the Amazon before changing transport or condensation.

Rejected run 97's overstrong stationary pressure and restored run 96's 0.12 response. Replaced both surface-only moisture transport and the arbitrary surface-to-500 hPa wind blend with a diagnostic 850 hPa wind derived from sea-level pressure and hypsometric thickness over a 150 km physical stencil. Orographic uplift and legacy downwind climate operations now use that same moisture-bearing lower-tropospheric flow.

Rejected run 98's diagnostic 850 hPa transport because it broadened rainfall but degraded spatial skill and left the South American monsoon dry. Restored run 96's better-directed surface moisture flow and changed only the initial land soil reservoir from empty to full 80 mm field capacity. This tests whether the stabilized hydrology still converges into a dry attractor from an unphysical dry start.

Full 365-day monthly-interpolated column hydrology; uniform-RH stratiform, terrain-attributed orographic, and convergence-plus-evaporation convective precipitation; pressure-aware moisture capacity; field-capacity soil initialization and separate atmospheric/soil spinup convergence.

Full-resolution two-layer hydrology with conservative boundary/free-troposphere moisture exchange, moist adjustment, diagnostic cloud fraction, falling-precipitation re-evaporation, rain/snow phase, finite snow storage, melt, infiltration, runoff, pressure/gravity-aware surface exchange, and floating-point transport/rainfall.

Reduced-resolution rainfall-shape iteration: 512x257 two-layer hydrology with conservative tropical background moisture diffusion and a two-pass area-weighted convergence footprint; retains seasonal ITCZ migration and continental moisture transport.

Reduced-resolution rainfall-shape iteration: run 102 tropical background moisture diffusion and conservative convergence footprint plus a 35-percent seasonally moving zonal-scale convergence blend to restore coherent ITCZ and storm-track envelopes while retaining local continental transport.

Reduced-resolution rainfall-shape iteration: conservative tropical background diffusion and two-pass convergence footprint, with slow free-tropospheric stratiform conversion beginning at 88-percent relative humidity to restore broad rain envelopes while retaining two-layer inland transport and falling-precipitation re-evaporation.

Reduced-resolution rainfall-shape iteration: run 104 progressive stratiform onset plus free-tropospheric moisture transport using 35-percent of the resolved upper-wind departure from surface flow, targeting run 100-scale rain envelopes while retaining two-layer inland penetration.

Reduced-resolution coastal-rainfall iteration: 65-percent upper-wind departure for free-tropospheric moisture, 15-percent low-level land transport drag to create conservative coast-crossing convergence, 88-percent stratiform onset, tropical background mixing, and the two-pass convergence footprint.

ExoPlaSim-derived reduced-grid hydrology: T42-like 128-cell moisture grid, continuous Kuo humidity and buoyancy closure, elevated accession, shallow and dry convection, scale-selective damping, deterministic synoptic and coastal weather phases, resolution-normalized orography with retained subgrid relief, and bounded latent-heating/cloud-radiative memory.

Run 107 physics plus finite-area, cell-centred polar cap geometry: no point cells at +/-90 degrees, conservative cap-to-midlatitude transport and eddy exchange, preventing polar moisture concentration.

Run 108 plus spectral-grid polar regularity: meridional transport tapers to zero across 72-88 degrees, deep/shallow convection and forced uplift taper across 55-75 degrees, and sea-ice evaporation is strongly suppressed.

Run 109 with timestep-aware polar flux regularity: meridional transport now tapers from 60 degrees and is zero by 72 degrees, preventing the multi-day reduced-grid step from saturating poleward transport into cap cells.
Run 110 plus consistent polar closure of transient-eddy moisture diffusion, eliminating the remaining numerical moisture-refill path into cold cap cells.
Diagnostic repeat of run 111 with internal latitude-row precipitation, evaporation, and vapour reporting to isolate the polar cap rainfall source.
Run 112 with the diagnosed final polar fix: scale-selective vapour and convergence damping now obeys the same high-latitude no-flux boundary as advection and eddy exchange.

Run 113 with the high-wavenumber filter rewritten as positivity-preserving zonal diffusion plus pairwise area-conservative meridional exchange, removing the global rescale that amplified trace polar vapour.
ExoPlaSim hydrology: polar transport budget diagnostic
ExoPlaSim hydrology: polar transport stage diagnostic
ExoPlaSim hydrology: conservative adjacent meridional moisture flux
ExoPlaSim mechanisms complete; conservative adjacent meridional flux; final 512 px baseline
